framework.name: EU AI Act
framework.summary: EU law on artificial intelligence for organisations that build, sell or use AI systems in the EU. The heaviest duties cover high-risk uses such as credit scoring and life and health insurance pricing. Check whether and how it applies to you.

groups.title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance

requirements.title: Staff and others operating AI systems for the organisation have sufficient AI literacy.
No AI system is offered or used for any practice the Act prohibits.
An Annex III system is classed not high-risk only under a listed condition and without profiling.
Providers document why an Annex III system is not high-risk before releasing it.
A risk management system runs through the whole life of a high-risk AI system.
Training, validation and test data for high-risk AI is governed, relevant and representative.
Technical documentation showing a high-risk system meets the requirements exists before release and stays current.
High-risk AI systems are built to log events automatically throughout their lifetime.
High-risk AI systems come with clear instructions so deployers can interpret and use their output.
High-risk AI systems are designed so that people can oversee them effectively while in use.
High-risk AI systems reach appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle.
Providers of high-risk AI systems run a documented quality management system.
Providers correct, withdraw or recall a non-conforming high-risk system and inform the supply chain.
Importers check a high-risk system's conformity assessment, documentation and marking before placing it on the market.
Distributors check a high-risk system's CE marking, declaration and instructions before making it available.
Deployers take technical and organisational measures to use high-risk systems as their instructions say.
Deployers assign human oversight to competent, trained people with the authority and support needed.
Deployers ensure input data they control is relevant and representative for the intended purpose.
Deployers monitor high-risk systems, suspend risky use and report serious incidents without delay.
Deployers keep the automatic logs of a high-risk system they control for at least six months.
Employers inform workers and their representatives before using a high-risk system at work.
Deployers use the provider's instructions to carry out any required data protection impact assessment.
Deployers tell people when an Annex III system makes or helps make decisions about them.
Public-service, credit-scoring and insurance-pricing deployers assess the impact on fundamental rights before use.
High-risk AI systems pass the required conformity assessment before they are released.
Providers draw up and keep a signed EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk system.
Providers affix the CE marking visibly, legibly and indelibly to conforming high-risk systems.
Providers register Annex III high-risk systems in the EU database before release.
Providers also register Annex III systems they have judged not to be high-risk.
Providers make sure people know when they are interacting with an AI system, unless obvious.
Providers mark synthetic audio, image, video and text output as AI-generated in machine-readable form.
Deployers tell people exposed to emotion recognition or biometric categorisation that it is running.
Deployers disclose deep fakes, and AI-generated text published on matters of public interest.
Providers collect and analyse data on how high-risk systems perform after release.
Providers report serious incidents involving high-risk systems to market surveillance authorities on time.
Deployers explain the AI's role and main reasons to people significantly affected by its decisions.
